name: Reissner-Nordström-anti-de Sitter Black Hole
description: A charged black hole in anti-de Sitter space, the static, spherically symmetric solution of the Einstein-Maxwell equations with a negative cosmological constant. It has an inner horizon and an event horizon inside a timelike boundary at infinity, and at fixed charge its small and large black holes behave as the liquid and the gas of a van der Waals fluid do.
convention: The Schwarzschild radius is $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, the charge radius $r_q$ has $r_q^2 = Q^2G/(4\pi\epsilon_0c^4)$, and the anti-de Sitter radius $L$, a length, fixes the cosmological constant through $\Lambda = -3/L^2$. The horizons $r_- < r_+$ are the two positive roots of $1 - r_s/r + r_q^2/r^2 + r^2/L^2$. We keep factors of $c$ explicit.
history: What does an electric charge do to a black hole that lives in a box? Anti-de Sitter space makes the box: its gravitational potential turns back every particle with rest mass, and Stephen Hawking and Don Page found in 1983 that a large black hole inside it stays in stable equilibrium with its own radiation [hawking1983]. Put the charge of Hans Reissner and Gunnar Nordström's black hole on theirs and the metric function is $$f(r) = 1 - \frac{r_s}{r} + \frac{r_q^2}{r^2} + \frac{r^2}{L^2}$$ [reissner1916, nordstrom1918, chamblin1999]. It vanishes at an inner horizon $r_-$ and at an event horizon $r_+$ [stuchlik2002]. The hole radiates at the temperature $$T = \frac{\hbar c}{4\pi k_B}\left(\frac{1}{r_+} - \frac{r_q^2}{r_+^3} + \frac{3r_+}{L^2}\right),$$ which is zero where the two horizons meet [chamblin1999]. By 1996 Jorma Louko and Stephen Winters-Hilt had its thermodynamics from the Hamiltonian of the spherically symmetric theory, entropy and all: a quarter of the area of the horizon in Planck units [louko1996].¶Charge equal to mass, $r_q = r_s/2$, marks the coldest Reissner-Nordström black hole in flat space, and that hole is supersymmetric [romans1992]. With a negative cosmological constant the same relation makes $f = (1 - r_q/r)^2 + r^2/L^2$, which is positive everywhere, so Larry Romans's supersymmetric solution of 1992 has no horizon and its singularity is naked [romans1992, chamblin1999]. A horizon needs more mass than that, and the cold hole, where $r_-$ and $r_+$ coincide, has $r_s > 2r_q$ and no supersymmetry [chamblin1999]. Its horizon still has an area, so at zero temperature the hole keeps its entropy [chamblin1999].¶Where does the charge come from? From rotation in dimensions we do not see [chamblin1999]. Spin the seven sphere of eleven dimensional supergravity equally in its four planes, and in four dimensions the rotation is this electric charge: that was the observation of Andrew Chamblin, Roberto Emparan, Clifford Johnson, and Robert Myers in 1999 [chamblin1999]. Gravity in anti-de Sitter space is a field theory on its boundary, by Juan Maldacena's conjecture, and here the theory is the one on a stack of M2 branes, hot and carrying a charge density [maldacena1998, chamblin1999]. Hold the electric potential between the horizon and infinity fixed, which fixes the ratio $r_q/r_+$, and with that ratio below one the four found Hawking and Page's picture again: anti-de Sitter space at low temperature and a large black hole above a transition [chamblin1999]. With the ratio above one a black hole is preferred at every temperature [chamblin1999].¶Fix the charge and the hole behaves like a fluid [chamblin1999]. Below the critical charge $r_q = L/6$ three black holes share one temperature, a small one, an unstable middle one, and a large one, and as the temperature rises the small hole jumps to the large one with a release of latent heat [chamblin1999]. Above the critical charge the small hole grows into the large one with no jump [chamblin1999]. Chamblin and his coauthors called the two "like the liquid phase and the gaseous phase, respectively", with the charge in the role of the fluid's temperature and $1/T$ in the role of its pressure [chamblin1999]. Thirteen years later David Kubizňák and Robert Mann completed the analogy by reading the cosmological constant itself as a pressure, $P = 3c^4/(8\pi GL^2)$, and the horizon radius as the volume per molecule, $v = 2\ell_P^2r_+$ with $\ell_P$ the Planck length [kubiznak2012]. Their critical point has $P_cv_c/k_BT_c = 3/8$, as every van der Waals fluid has, and the same critical exponents [kubiznak2012].¶A charged hole in a box can also lose its charge to a wave [basu2010, bosch2016]. A wave of a charged scalar field that scatters off the hole can come back stronger, carrying off charge and mass, and the reflecting boundary of anti-de Sitter space sends it in again and again [bosch2016]. On a computer, Pablo Bosch, Stephen Green, and Luis Lehner followed this superradiant instability to its end in 2016: the hole sheds charge and mass until the wave stops growing, and the final state is a stable black hole with scalar hair [bosch2016]. For small holes that end state had been constructed analytically in 2010 by Pallab Basu, Jyotirmoy Bhattacharya, Sayantani Bhattacharyya, R. Loganayagam, Shiraz Minwalla, and V. Umesh, as a small Reissner-Nordström-anti-de Sitter black hole inside a condensate of the charged field that fills the box [basu2010].¶And inside? Beyond the inner horizon the singularity is timelike, and the conformal diagram is a tower of the same six regions repeated without end, which Dominic Brecher, Jianyang He, and Moshe Rozali drew in 2005 for the hole in five dimensions [brecher2005]. Its boundaries and its singularities cannot both be drawn as straight lines [brecher2005]. The inner horizon is a Cauchy horizon, and outside the hole waves die away only logarithmically, far more slowly than around a black hole in flat space [kehle2020]. Christoph Kehle proved in 2020 that linear scalar waves stay bounded inside the hole all the same, and extend continuously across the Cauchy horizon [kehle2020]. Outside, Zdeněk Stuchlík and Stanislav Hledík mapped the geodesics in 2002 and drew embedding diagrams of the equatorial plane, and found a region of stable circular orbits around every black hole of the family [stuchlik2002].

related.text: This black hole with no charge, $r_q = 0$. The inner horizon goes, and with it the small stable black hole of the fixed charge ensemble [chamblin1999].
This black hole with no cosmological constant, $L \to \infty$. The timelike boundary at infinity goes, and both horizons stay.
The charged black hole with a positive cosmological constant. A cosmological horizon stands where this one has a timelike boundary [romans1992].
This spacetime with the mass and the charge taken out, $r_s = r_q = 0$. The timelike boundary at infinity stays.
Black holes of anti-de Sitter space with flat and hyperbolic horizons. The hyperbolic hole of negative mass has an inner horizon and a conformal diagram like this one's [mann1997negative, brill1997].

Anti-de Sitter space of four dimensions times a 7-sphere. Charged black holes of anti-de Sitter space solve the gauged supergravity of that compactification, their charge coming from a rotation in the directions of the sphere [chamblin1999, awada1983].

coordinates.name: Static Spherical

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(2r^4 + L^2\,r\,r_s - 2L^2\,r_q^2\right)\left(r^4 + L^2\,r^2 - L^2\,r\,r_s + L^2\,r_q^2\right)}{2L^4\,r^5}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{2r^4 + L^2\,r\,r_s - 2L^2\,r_q^2}{2r\left(r^4 + L^2\,r^2 - L^2\,r\,r_s + L^2\,r_q^2\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r^4 + L^2\,r^2 - L^2\,r\,r_s + L^2\,r_q^2}{L^2\,r}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^4 + L^2\,r^2 - L^2\,r\,r_s + L^2\,r_q^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{L^2\,r}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(u, r, \theta, \phi)$, with the retarded time $u = ct - r_*$ a length, where $dr_*/dr = \left(1 - r_s/r + r_q^2/r^2 + r^2/L^2\right)^{-1}$ and $r_* = 0$ at $r = 0$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(2r^4 + L^2\,r\,r_s - 2L^2\,r_q^2\right)\left(r^4 + L^2\,r^2 - L^2\,r\,r_s + L^2\,r_q^2\right)}{2L^4\,r^5}\dot{u}^2 + \dfrac{2r^4 + L^2\,r\,r_s - 2L^2\,r_q^2}{L^2\,r^3}\dot{u}\dot{r} - \dfrac{r^4 + L^2\,r^2 - L^2\,r\,r_s + L^2\,r_q^2}{L^2\,r}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^4 + L^2\,r^2 - L^2\,r\,r_s + L^2\,r_q^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{L^2\,r}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \phi)$, with the advanced time $v = ct + r_*$ a length, where $dr_*/dr = \left(1 - r_s/r + r_q^2/r^2 + r^2/L^2\right)^{-1}$ and $r_* = 0$ at $r = 0$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(2r^4 + L^2\,r\,r_s - 2L^2\,r_q^2\right)\left(r^4 + L^2\,r^2 - L^2\,r\,r_s + L^2\,r_q^2\right)}{2L^4\,r^5}\dot{v}^2 - \dfrac{2r^4 + L^2\,r\,r_s - 2L^2\,r_q^2}{L^2\,r^3}\dot{v}\dot{r} - \dfrac{r^4 + L^2\,r^2 - L^2\,r\,r_s + L^2\,r_q^2}{L^2\,r}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^4 + L^2\,r^2 - L^2\,r\,r_s + L^2\,r_q^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{L^2\,r}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0
